title: Why? #3: why |2A| is not 2|A| (a determinant is an area) → NDA 2025 (II) Q44 (47 s, continuous motion)

captions.instagram:
Why? #3 · Why is |2A| not 2|A|? 🔷

The rows of a 2×2 matrix are two arrows, and its determinant is the area of the parallelogram they make. A = [3 1; 1 2] → |A| = 3·2 − 1·1 = 5.
Double one row: one side stretches → 2 copies → area 10.
Double the other row too (that's 2A): 4 copies → |2A| = 20 = 4|A|, not 2|A|.
For an n×n matrix: |mA| = mⁿ|A|.

NDA 2025 (II) asked exactly this (Maths Q44): Statement I: det(mX) = mⁿ det(X). Statement II: multiplying one row by m multiplies det by m. Answer (a): both true, and II explains I.

Why? #3 · Why is |2A| not 2|A|? 🔷

A determinant is an area: the rows of A are two arrows and |A| is the parallelogram between them. Doubling one row stretches one side (area × 2); 2A doubles both rows, so the area goes × 4: |2A| = 4|A|. For n×n: |mA| = mⁿ|A|.

NDA 2025 (II) Maths Q44: Statement II (one row × m ⇒ det × m) explains Statement I (det(mX) = mⁿ det X) → (a).
